title: Pex / WMS Real-time Event Buffering + WebSocket Support
description: Implement two v2 feature groups: (a) Pex/WMS named WebSocket connections with per-account JSONL event buffering and drain operations, and (b) generic named WebSocket connections (ws group) with connect, send, listen, and close. Both groups integrate with the trace session system for audit trail.
prerequisiteState: All v1 stories (1-8) completed. Trace system (TraceWriter, TraceSession) is fully working. OAuth2 (Story 10) should also be complete for full account support.
goal: pex connect opens a Pex/WMS WebSocket and buffers events to a per-account JSONL file. pex drain atomically reads and truncates the buffer. ws connect/send/listen/close manage generic named WebSocket connections. All pex buffer files exclude token values.
scope: Create src/ZapiCli.Core/Pex/PexTraceEntry.cs as a sealed record with Seq, Type (=>"pex"), Session, Timestamp, Account, RelatedApiSeq, HandlerClass, CallbackMethod, Payload
Create src/ZapiCli.Core/Pex/PexBufferWriter.cs: writes pex events to <configDir>/pex-buffer/<account>.jsonl; token values must never appear in buffer files

Create src/ZapiCli/Commands/PexCommands.cs: PexConnectCommand (opens Pex/WMS WebSocket), PexSendCommand (--message req), PexDrainCommand (atomically reads and truncates buffer; returns JSON array; appends PexTraceEntry to active trace session), PexClearCommand (discards buffer), PexListenCommand (streams JSONL to stdout, blocking), PexCloseCommand
pex connect uses account's PAT/OAuth token for WebSocket authentication; ZohoCorp block applies
pex drain appends a PexTraceEntry to the active trace session for each event drained (if a session is active)

Create src/ZapiCli/Commands/WsCommands.cs: WsConnectCommand (--url req, --name req, --account optional), WsSendCommand (--name req, --message req), WsListenCommand (--name req, blocking JSONL stream), WsCloseCommand (--name req)
ws connect validates the target URL against the host allowlist (same SSRF check as ApiClient)
Register pex commands under 'pex' branch and ws commands under 'ws' branch in Program.cs

Unit tests: pex drain returns buffered events and truncates buffer; pex drain with active session appends PexTraceEntry; pex buffer files contain no token values; ws connect with non-allowlisted host → HOST_NOT_ALLOWED
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors and 0 warnings
pex connect opens a Pex/WMS WebSocket for the resolved account
pex drain atomically reads and empties the buffer; returns events as JSON array; appends PexTraceEntry to active trace session if one exists
pex clear discards the buffer without returning events
pex listen streams events as JSONL to stdout (blocking until Ctrl+C)
pex send --message <m> sends a raw message over the Pex socket
Token values do not appear in any pex buffer file
ws connect with a non-Zoho URL → HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, exit 1
ws send/listen/close work against a named connection
contextForAgent: Read prd.json FR-012 for the Pex/WMS design and FR-014 for the WebSocket design. The pex drain command must be atomic — read all events, then truncate the file; agents depend on this to prevent event loss. PexTraceEntry is a distinct trace entry type from ApiTraceEntry (typeValue='pex'). The ws group validates URLs against the host allowlist just as ApiClient does (SSRF prevention applies equally to WebSocket connections).

openItems.defaultAssumption: Use the account's bearer token (PAT or OAuth) in the WebSocket handshake Authorization header. Consult Zoho Cliq Pex API documentation for the exact authentication mechanism.

Read all lines from the buffer file into memory, then truncate the file to zero bytes (using FileStream with FileMode.Truncate or File.WriteAllText with empty string). Perform under a file lock to prevent concurrent drain/write races.

sourceReferences: tech_spec/prd.md (§ FR-012 Pex/WMS real-time, § FR-014 WebSocket, § commandTree v2additions)
